findings.title: The generic failed-run scenario still names the handoff commit for every launched run, a pair half included
findings.recommendation: The walk qualified the failure ROW of `A recorded runner launches the external review` (a blind pair's external half names the pair's REVIEWED COMMIT), and the ADDED requirement's scenario `A failed re-run's fallback names the reviewed commit` asserts that output, but the same requirement's scenario `A failed run falls back to paste` still says, for any launched runner that exits non-zero, 'the line naming the repository and the handoff commit in place of the removed worktree'. For a pair's re-run the two scenarios give different outputs for one input — the defect F3 fixed for the byte-for-byte scenario. Qualify that THEN the way the row is qualified ('the handoff commit — for a blind pair's external half, the pair's REVIEWED COMMIT —'), or guard its WHEN with 'outside a blind pair'.

walk_entry.title: A failed RE-RUN's paste fallback sends the reviewer to the re-run's handoff commit, which holds the committed fresh partner

findings.title: The fresh re-run row narrows the state to read to the change's files, leaving a system-mode fresh re-run reading the code at HEAD
findings.recommendation: The walk restored the reviewed-commit brief, but the row says the brief names the REVIEWED COMMIT 'as the state to read — the change's files read at that commit'. A system-mode fresh pass reviews the code and the commit range too (orbit-review's system read list), so a brief built to this row would pin the artifacts to the reviewed commit and leave the code at HEAD — the divergence external W3 named, surviving for system mode. Say 'the repository read at that commit' (the change's files and, in system mode, the code and the commit range ending there), and carry the same words into design D6 and task 4.1.

findings.title: The change's metadata changed after the base pass and no walk entry lists it
findings.recommendation: The residual check lists .openspec.yaml as changed since the external pass's commit, outside every entry's edit record. It is the base-fingerprint stamp for the `Single-voiced canonical-next computation` block the F1 resolution added — a record gap, not a defect: name the stamp in that entry's ripple record on the next walk, or let this note stand as the record.

commentary: Graded the fourteen resolved entries of both walks over each entry's file and ripple record, re-reading every edited block in full rather than the introduced strings alone. Twelve hold. The two that do not share one shape: a walk repaired the site the finding named and stopped one site short — a second scenario of the same claim, and a dash clause that narrowed the rule it was restoring. The two stale calls in the external log were re-checked: both converge with the fresh log's entries by site and claim; the CRITICAL's re-derivation against the repaired spec holds (save refused under --launch L, and the run not a re-run once an apply is later than L).
